summary: The organizer's site gives the Grand Final as 2026-11-21 (not 22), at the Canadian War Museum, 5:30-8:00 PM EST. Sunset on 22 Nov is about 4:26 PM, so that slot is after dark. The site does not say when the flight happens, so ask the organizers. The only challenge text is "Live position hold without GNSS using Visual-Inertial Odometry"; no altitude, hardware or limits are published. Climate normals (ECCC, CYOW, 1981-2010) give a November mean wind of 13.8 km/h from the west at 10 m. Estimated mean wind at 100-120 m is about 19-25 km/h (rule-based estimate). Daily high is about +5 C and low about -2 C. Snow depth is 1 cm or more on about 5-6 days of 30; no day-specific snow probability was found. CYR537 (0.4 mile radius, surface to 3000 ft) covers Parliament Hill; the museum appears to lie outside it (inference). The legal ceiling is 122 m AGL, and an event flight probably has a lower cap set by the organizers (inference). The team's compute-board and UART notes were not confirmed by any source.

Altitude cap and the drift/stability limits (limits arrive 72 h before the event)
Gust statistics and wind direction spread for Ottawa in late November
Day-specific snow-on-ground probability for 21-22 Nov and median date of first lasting snow cover
Exact airspace class and limits at the museum; the NRC/NAV CANADA drone tool returned HTTP 403
Barometer model of the Orqa flight controller and its temperature drift; lens fog and frost data
Current ground state at LeBreton Flats (construction, snow clearing, event tents); no imagery was retrieved
1991-2020 wind and snow normals (the API held only 1981-2010 for these)

recommendations: Email the organizers now: confirm the date is 21 Nov, the flight time slot, lighting (night or day), indoor or outdoor, altitude cap, and camera and compute specs.
If any flight is after sunset, add dark and low-light runs to the sim (noise, motion blur, low contrast, no texture) and test whether the Justice D camera sees anything.
Add sim cases for river-filled views, uniform lawn, and a thin snow cover; log tracked-point count against position error.
Test with wind: use hourly mean 14 km/h at 10 m and about 20-25 km/h at 100 m, with gust cases of 50-60 km/h; closed-loop with drone dynamics if possible.
Add long moving shadow cases (sun 24 deg at noon, setting about 4:26 PM) to the textured and aerial-photo sims.
Procedure: pre-warm batteries, keep the camera lens dry, let the baro and board warm up before arming, and take a baro and temperature log on the ground before flight.
Check the NAV CANADA/NRC drone tool and the Canada Flight Supplement in a browser; the organizers hold the permissions but the altitude cap should be asked for.
